conflict_topics: safety of open bowl / ability to move
aisle obstruction / impact on adjacent diner
timing / how long each person will occupy the seat
dialogue_quality_notes: Alex repeatedly invokes the tissue packet across rounds to assert a short-term reservation claim.
Jamie consistently gives practical safety reasons (open bowl will spill) for not moving immediately.
Casey contributes relevant spatial constraint (aisle narrowing) that affects feasible accommodations.
Robin's decision to take the alternative seat changed the practical options and increased pressure on Jamie/Alex.
Resolution occurs through a concrete action (Jamie finishing and leaving), not mere verbal agreement.
evaluation.final_reason: Jamie finished her meal and voluntarily left the disputed seat; Alex then took the seat, resolving the incompatible claims.
position_change_notes: Jamie: initially refused to move due to safety concerns, later committed to and carried out leaving after finishing the bowl (softened position then concession).
Alex: consistently demanded access based on the reservation claim and time needs; accepted outcome once Jamie left and then took the seat (position maintained until practical resolution).
Casey: voiced concern about aisle narrowing if Jamie stood; did not change position but introduced a constraint that limited proposed accommodations.
Robin: acted by taking the alternative seat, changing the available options for Alex and Jamie.
No participant reversed to an earlier position without an expressed practical reason; changes were driven by observable conditions (bowl finished, alternative seat taken).

round_scores.evidence: Alex claims the tissue packet reserved the seat and demands Jamie leave within ~4 minutes; Jamie rejects absolute priority and says she needs ~8 minutes to finish and won't move while the bowl is unsafe.
Alex reiterates the reservation claim and gives a 4-minute ultimatum; Casey adds that if Jamie stands it will narrow the aisle, introducing an additional incompatible practical constraint.

Alex presses for an immediate choice; Jamie refuses to move the open bowl but then commits to finishing in roughly three minutes and leaving right after, reducing but not yet eliminating the incompatibility.

An alternative seat appears but is taken by Robin; Alex's deadline tightens (now ~2 minutes) while Jamie still occupies the disputed seat with several spoonfuls left, keeping opposing positions and practical blockage.
Jamie finishes the bowl, announces she will leave, then physically leaves the seat and Alex takes it; the substantive seat dispute is settled by Jamie leaving.
Two minutes later no standing seat-seekers remain and Alex occupies the disputed seat; no substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: A physical marker (tissue packet) functions as a social claim but does not create absolute priority when it conflicts with safety and ongoing use.
Practical constraints (open bowl risk, narrow aisle) limited Jamie's feasible options and justified temporary refusal to move.
Availability and timely occupation of an alternative seat (Robin taking it) materially escalated stakes for Alex.
The dispute was resolved when the occupier completed the activity (finished meal), showing how temporal commitments can resolve space conflicts without explicit compromise.
